rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~97% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~93%; BoE Dec ~82%; BoJ Dec ~85%; BoC Dec ~80%; RBA Dec hold ~99%
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays all but certain. Soft French and Spanish inflation leaves a December European Central Bank hike likely but weakens the case for more after it. The Bank of England, Bank of Japan and Bank of Canada are all still expected to hike in December.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: China industrial profits Oct +20.1% y/y; US goods trade gap Oct −$149.5B (fcst −$135.9B); Germany unemployment +9K (fcst +5K); Canada Q3 current account +C$4.5B (fcst C$9.5B)
rows.read: Chinese factory profits grew at their fastest in five months, good news for Australia. The US goods trade gap widened sharply as imports of artificial intelligence equipment surged, a drag on US growth this quarter. German unemployment rose more than expected.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: France CPI Nov 2.9% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Spain CPI Nov 4.1% (fcst 4.7%), core 2.6%; Tokyo core CPI Nov 2.9% (fcst 3.0%), ex-food and energy 2.5%; US core PCE Oct 3.3%; Australia CPI Oct 4.9%
rows.read: Inflation slowed far more than expected in France and Spain as fuel got cheaper. Tokyo's core inflation reached a 16-month high but cooled underneath. US and Australian inflation still run hot, which keeps their central banks leaning toward higher rates.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Gold ~$3,646 (+2.2%), morning high ~$3,690; Israel security cabinet meeting on Iran cancelled, no decision; USD/CHF ~0.836 (+0.24%); AUD/USD +0.30%
rows.read: Asian shares rose for a second day, but fear of new Israeli strikes on Iran sent money into gold. The franc did not share the gain. Thin post-Thanksgiving trading can make moves look bigger than they are.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: NZ final count: coalition 65 of 130 seats, 66 needed (ABC News); S&P France review Fri Nov 27; US Section 301 tariff proposals on 14 economies, comments due Jan 5 (USTR)
rows.read: New Zealand's final election count left the governing coalition one seat short of a majority, so it must win over a smaller party or face a new vote. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating late on Friday, November 27.
